mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST QoQ < -10%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for three consecutive months, combined with accelerating average hourly earnings (implied by PAYEMS growth outpacing labor force growth), signals a tight labor market that increases input costs and inflationary pressure, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as markets anticipate higher corporate pricing power.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% for three consecutive months AND PAYEMS growth outpaces labor force expansion
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods of UNRATE < 3.5% for three months and strong PAYEMS growth.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings visibility and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when INDPRO falls by more than 0.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth expectations for consumer-facing sectors and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when RSAFS declines by more than 1% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recession signals an aggressive monetary easing, which supports risk assets by lowering borrowing costs and boosting liquidity, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when FEDFUNDS < 1% and UNRATE > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) of more than 0.4 percentage points, combined with a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000, signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE rises by more than 0.4pp and PAYEMS falls by more than 100,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for three consecutive quarters signals economic stagnation, which reduces corporate profit expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when GDPC1 annualized < 1% for three consecutive quarters.
